from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Periodic Oscillations", [
            "Waves are defined by amplitude and frequency.", 
            "Phase shifts determine wave position.", 
            "Multiple waves combine into complex shapes."
        ])
        
        # Setup common objects
        ax = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Waves are defined by amplitude and frequency.

        self.place_in_area(ax, *graph_area, scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(wave, *graph_area, scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(ax), Create(wave))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Phase shifts determine wave position.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        shifted_wave = ax.plot(lambda x: np.sin(PI * (x - 0.5)), color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(shifted_wave, *graph_area, scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Transform(wave, shifted_wave))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Multiple waves combine into complex shapes.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        complex_wave = ax.plot(lambda x: np.sin(PI * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(3 * PI * x), color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(complex_wave, *graph_area, scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Transform(wave, complex_wave))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Time to Frequency", [
            "Time domain shows events occurring.", 
            "Frequency domain reveals signal DNA.", 
            "Integrals match signals to reference frequencies."
        ])
        
        # Create visual elements
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * PI * t) + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * PI * t), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        comp1 = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * PI * t), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#00FFFF")
        comp2 = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.3 * np.sin(5 * PI * t), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#FF00FF")
        
        freq_axis = Line(start=np.array([-2, -2, 0]), end=np.array([2, -2, 0]), color="#FF8800")
        amp_spike1 = Line(start=np.array([-1, -2, 0]), end=np.array([-1, -1, 0]), color="#FF8800")
        amp_spike2 = Line(start=np.array([1, -2, 0]), end=np.array([1, -0.6, 0]), color="#FF8800")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(wave, "A1", "C6")
        self.play(Create(wave))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(wave.copy(), comp1),
            ReplacementTransform(wave.copy(), comp2),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Summing back
        self.play(
            FadeOut(comp1), FadeOut(comp2),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF8800")
        self.play(
            Create(freq_axis),
            Create(amp_spike1),
            Create(amp_spike2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The transform multiplies signal by sine waves.",
            "Correlation results highlight frequency presence.",
            "Matching waves isolate signal energy.",
            "Non-matching frequencies cancel out.",
            "This process sifts hidden components."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fourier Transform Integral", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"F(\omega) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t) e^{-i\omega t} dt", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Highlighting 't' in the formula
        t_part = formula[0][8]
        self.play(t_part.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Highlighting complex exponential
        exp_part = formula[0][10:15]
        self.play(exp_part.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF8800"))
        # Integral sign and limits
        int_part = formula[0][3:6]
        self.play(int_part.animate.set_color("#FF8800"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Whole result part
        res_part = formula[0][0:2]
        self.play(res_part.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Digital World", [
            "Fourier Transform powers modern digital tech.",
            "Frequency identification allows data compression.",
            "We discard imperceptible frequencies efficiently.",
            "Compression reduces file size drastically.",
            "Audio quality remains effectively preserved."
        ])
        
        # Define visual objects
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(4*x) + 0.5*np.sin(10*x), x_range=[-3, 3], color=CYAN_COLOR)
        samples = VGroup(*[Dot(point=[x, np.sin(4*x) + 0.5*np.sin(10*x), 0], color=CYAN_COLOR, radius=0.03) for x in np.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, 50)])
        
        # Assets
        mic = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microphone.svg")
        speaker = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speaker.svg")
        
        compressed_samples = VGroup(*[Dot(point=[x, np.sin(4*x), 0], color=MAGENTA_COLOR, radius=0.03) for x in np.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, 20)])
        reconstructed = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(4*x), x_range=[-3, 3], color=CYAN_COLOR)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(CYAN_COLOR))
        self.place_at_grid(mic, "B2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(mic))
        self.place_in_area(wave, "A3", "C6")
        self.play(Create(wave))
        self.place_in_area(samples, "D3", "F6")
        self.play(Create(samples))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(MAGENTA_COLOR))
        self.play(FadeOut(wave), FadeOut(samples), FadeOut(mic))
        self.place_in_area(compressed_samples, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Create(compressed_samples))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN_COLOR))
        self.play(compressed_samples.animate.set_color(CYAN_COLOR))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(MAGENTA_COLOR))
        self.play(compressed_samples.animate.scale(0.7))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(CYAN_COLOR))
        self.place_at_grid(speaker, "B5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(speaker))
        self.place_in_area(reconstructed, "A1", "F6")
        self.play(Create(reconstructed), FadeOut(compressed_samples))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Prism Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a prism splits white light into a rainbow of colors, the Fourier Transform splits a complex signal into its fundamental sine and cosine frequencies.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'smoothie' vs. its ingredients: If a signal is a smoothie, the Fourier Transform identifies the exact amounts of strawberry, banana, and yogurt used to make it.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Periodic Oscillations
sections.content: Briefly revisit the components of a wave: Amplitude (height), Frequency (cycles per second), and Phase (shift). Use a graphical animation showing multiple sine waves layering to form a complex 'jagged' wave.
sections.example: Visualizing a clock hand rotating: As it spins faster, the frequency increases, forming the basis of a circular motion that represents our sine waves.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Moving from Time to Frequency
sections.content: Explain the transition from the Time Domain (where we see events happening over time) to the Frequency Domain (where we see the 'DNA' of the signal). Focus on the integral formula as a process of matching the signal against a 'reference frequency'.
sections.example: An audio recording of a bird chirping: In the time domain, it's a messy waveform; in the frequency domain, it becomes a distinct spike at the frequency of the chirp.

sections.title: The Fourier Transform Integral: Decoding the Signature
sections.content: Explain the concept of correlation: the transform 'multiplies' the signal by a pure sine wave and integrates. If they match, the result is high; if they don't, it cancels out. This 'sifts' out the hidden frequencies.
sections.example: A 'Lock and Key' animation: Imagine the Fourier transform as a set of master keys (sine waves of different sizes). Only the key that matches the frequency 'unlocks' the signal's energy at that spot.

sections.title: Application: The Digital World
sections.content: Show how the Fourier Transform is the engine behind modern technology. By identifying frequencies, we can compress data by removing frequencies humans can't hear or see.
sections.example: MP3 compression: The Fourier Transform identifies high-frequency sounds the human ear can't hear, allowing us to 'discard' them to make the file size smaller without affecting perceived audio quality.
